challenge.heading: Just a moment…
challenge.intro: Checking that you're a person and not a bot. This only takes a moment, and only happens once.
challenge.intro_turnstile: Please confirm you're a person to continue. This happens only once.
challenge.failed: That check didn't go through. Trying again…
challenge.noscript: Please turn on JavaScript to continue. It's only used for this one-time check.
challenge.footer: This site turns away scrapers and unwanted bots. Your browser keeps a cookie so you won't see this again.

overview.mode_help: Monitor only logs what Bouncer would do, without challenging or blocking anyone. A good way to start.
overview.week_empty: Nothing logged yet. Ordinary visitors are never logged, only bots and anything challenged or turned away.
overview.you_heading: Your address as Bouncer sees it
overview.you_public: {ip}. Visitors' addresses are coming through, so rate limits and network checks work.
overview.you_private: {ip} is a private address, so Flarum sits behind a reverse proxy and Bouncer can't see visitors' addresses yet. Until it can, rate limits, data-centre checks and search engine verification are skipped. Choose the header your proxy sets below.
overview.ip_header_label: Where your reverse proxy puts the visitor's address
overview.ip_header_help: Read only when a request comes from your own proxy (a private address, or one listed under Lists → Trusted proxies). Choose the header your proxy sets itself: with nginx, X-Forwarded-For if it uses $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for, X-Real-IP if it sets X-Real-IP to $remote_addr. A header your proxy only passes along can be forged by anyone.
overview.headers_seen: Your request to this page carried:
overview.headers_none: Your request to this page carried neither header.
overview.networks_cron: Refreshed weekly by Flarum's scheduler (php flarum schedule:run in cron), or now with the button.
overview.apcu_on: Rate counts are kept in APCu (shared memory).
overview.apcu_off: Rate counts are kept in Flarum's cache. With Redis that's fine; on the file cache, installing APCu makes them cheaper.

crawlers.intro: Choose which bots may read the forum. A blocked bot is turned away with a 403 and listed in robots.txt, so the polite ones stop asking. Real search engines (Google, Bing, Apple, Yandex, Baidu, Yahoo, Seznam, Petal) are verified by DNS and always let in; anything only claiming to be one is turned away.

kinds.assistant: AI assistants fetching a page for a person

kind_help.training: Collect pages to train AI models. Nothing comes back to your forum.
kind_help.search: Index pages to quote them in AI answers, with a link back.
kind_help.assistant: Fetch one page when someone asks an assistant about it.
kind_help.seo: Crawl for SEO tools' backlink and keyword databases.

crawlers.robots_help: Added after any robots.txt another extension serves, or to a simple one of Bouncer's own.
crawlers.ai_txt_label: Serve an ai.txt that opts the forum out of AI training
crawlers.check_ok: {file} is served by Flarum, so Bouncer's version is what crawlers get.
crawlers.check_bad: {file} isn't reaching Flarum (HTTP {status}): your web server answers it itself. Remove that rule (in nginx, a "location = /{file}" block, or a {file} file in public/) so Flarum can serve it.

rules.challenge_pow: Proof of work (built in, no third party)
rules.challenge_turnstile: Cloudflare Turnstile (uses your Turnstile extension's keys)
rules.turnstile_missing: Turnstile is chosen, but no Turnstile keys were found, so the proof of work is used. Set the keys in your Turnstile extension.
rules.difficulty_help: Each step doubles the work. At 16 a laptop takes about a tenth of a second and an older phone well under a second; scripts that can't run JavaScript never get through at any setting.
rules.everyone_help: Every guest solves a challenge before seeing anything. Signed-in members, verified search engines and allowed bots aren't affected.
rules.tools_label: HTTP libraries, scanners and headless browsers
rules.tools_help: curl, python-requests, Go and Java clients, Scrapy, headless Chrome, Puppeteer, Playwright and the like, and requests with no user agent at all.
rules.headers_label: Browsers missing the headers every real browser sends
rules.headers_help: No Accept-Language, or a recent Chrome or Firefox without its Sec-Fetch headers. Typical of scripts that borrow a browser's name.
rules.datacentre_help: Cloud and hosting providers, where scrapers rent their servers. People on a VPN may land here too, so this only ever challenges.
rules.fake_engines_label: Bots pretending to be a search engine
rules.fake_engines_help: A Googlebot or Bingbot whose address doesn't belong to Google or Microsoft.
rules.burst_challenge_label: Challenge an address above this many requests a minute
rules.burst_block_label: Refuse an address above this many requests a minute (HTTP 429)
rules.burst_help: Counts guests' page and API requests per address. 0 turns a limit off. Verified search engines are never counted.
rules.api_help: Guests' API requests get the same checks, answered in JSON. Signed-in members, API keys and apps with a token are never checked.
rules.log_days_label: Keep the log for this many days

lists.ips_help: One address or CIDR range per line (203.0.113.7, 198.51.100.0/24, 2001:db8::/32).
lists.agents_help: One piece of text per line, matched anywhere in the user agent, ignoring case.
lists.exempt_help: One path prefix per line, below the forum's address. Feeds, sitemaps and robots.txt are here by default so readers and crawlers can always fetch them.
lists.proxies_help: Addresses of reverse proxies or load balancers in front of Flarum, one per line. Private addresses (10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x, 127.x) are trusted already, and Cloudflare's ranges are recognised for CF-Connecting-IP.
lists.asns_help: AS numbers, separated by spaces or commas. Click Refresh now on the Overview tab afterwards.

log.search_placeholder: Search address, user agent or bot
